ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, two parallel long straight metal rails are fixed in a horizontal plane with a distance of $l$ between them. Two identical conductor rods AB and CD are placed on the rails perpendicularly, both with a length of $l$. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the rods and the rails is $\mu$, where the maximum static friction equals the kinetic friction. The entire setup is in a uniform magnetic field with a magnetic flux density of magnitude $B$ directed vertically downward. Starting at $t=0$, an external force is applied to rod AB, causing it to undergo uniform acceleration from rest towards the right, until the external force is removed at time $t=t_{1}$. At this time, the induced current in the rod is $i_{1}$. It is known that rod CD starts to move at time $t=t_{0}$ $(0<t_{0}<t_{1})$, and both rods maintain good contact with the rails throughout the motion. The mass of both rods is $m$, and their resistance is $R$. The resistance of the rails is negligible. The magnitude of gravitational acceleration is $g$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the acceleration of rod AB during its uniformly accelerated motion.
2. Calculate the speed of rod CD when the external force is removed.
3. After the external force is removed, rod CD comes to rest at time $t=t_{2}$. Determine the magnitude of the velocity of rod AB at this instant.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two mutually parallel horizontal metal rails, arranged one above the other; the conductor rod spanning the rails on the left is CD, and the conductor rod spanning the rails on the right is AB. A closed loop is formed between the two rods, and the arrow beside AB points to the right, indicating that AB moves to the right; the figure also marks the spacing between the two rails as l. The problem states that the magnetic field is vertically downward, the resistance of the rails is ignored, and the resistances of both rods are R. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and the figure, AB starts from rest and moves to the right with uniform acceleration. Let the magnitude of AB's acceleration in 0<t<t1 be a. First consider the stage 0<t<t0 in which CD has not yet moved; at this time v_CD=0, v_AB=at. The total resistance of the loop is 2R, and the magnitude of the induced electromotive force is Blv_AB, so the magnitude of the induced current is I=Blv_AB/(2R)=Blat/(2R). When CD just begins to move, the Ampere force BlI is just equal to the maximum static friction μmg, therefore Bl·Blat0/(2R)=μmg, solving gives a=2μmgR/(B^2l^2t0). At t=t1, the velocity of AB is v_AB(t1)=at1. At this time the induced current produced by the relative motion of the two rods is i1=Bl[v_AB(t1)-v_CD(t1)]/(2R), so v_CD(t1)=at1-2Ri1/(Bl). Substituting a gives v_CD(t1)=2μmgRt1/(B^2l^2t0)-2Ri1/(Bl). After the external force is removed, from t1 to t2, viewing the two rods as a whole, the magnetic forces appear in pairs between the two rods and the resultant forces cancel each other; when both rods move to the right, the kinetic friction forces are both to the left. Thus m dv_AB/dt + m dv_CD/dt = -2μmg, that is d(v_AB+v_CD)/dt=-2μg. Integration gives v_AB(t2)+v_CD(t2)=v_AB(t1)+v_CD(t1)-2μg(t2-t1). It is known that CD stops at t2, v_CD(t2)=0, therefore v_AB(t2)=v_AB(t1)+v_CD(t1)-2μg(t2-t1)=2at1-2Ri1/(Bl)-2μg(t2-t1). Substituting a, obtain v_AB(t2)=4μmgRt1/(B^2l^2t0)-2Ri1/(Bl)-2μg(t2-t1).
